blocks.text: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) and Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) The Two daughters of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Refuse to Accept Money Given to Them
The Incident of Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) and her Mother

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) reports that Qutaylah bint Abdul Uzza bin Abd Sa'd from the Banu Maalik bin Hisl tribe was still a Mushrik when she brought some gifts to her daughter Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) the daughter of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). The gifts included a type of badger (which the Arabs ate), some bread and some butter. However, (because her mother was not a Muslim) Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) refused to accept the gifts and even refused to allow her mother into her house. When (her sister) Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) asked Rasulullaah ﷺ about this, Allaah revealed the verse:

blocks.arabic_text: لَا يَنْهٰكُمُ اللّٰهُ عَنِ الَّذِيْنَ لَمْ يُقَاتِلُوْكُمْ فِي الدِّيْنِ وَلَمْ يُخْرِجُوْكُمْ مِّنْ دِيَارِكُمْ اَنْ تَبَرُّوْهُمْ وَتُقْسِطُوْا اِلَيْهِمْ اِنَّ اللّٰهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِيْنَ
blocks.text: Allaah does not forbid you from behaving cordially and justly towards those (Kuffaar) who do not fight you for (reason of your) religion and who do not drive you out from your homes. Verily Allaah loves those who are just.
Rasulullaah ﷺ then instructed Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) to accept her mother's gift and to allow her into her home.[^1]
The Incident of Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) and a Poor Lady

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) relates, "A poor lady once came to me with a gift. I however refused to accept it out of pity for her (because she needed it more than I did). Rasulullaah ﷺ then told me, "Why did you rather not accept her gift and give her something else in return? I think that you may have been looking down on her. Humble yourself, O Aa'isha because Allaah loves the humble ones and detests the proud ones."[^2]
